title: Objects can crash Godot if their script contains remove_and_delete_child() in multiple loops
body:
I'll let the project do the talking
http://www.mediafire.com/download/g34cr3uxtmq5rpr/Test.zip

Basically, this contains a turret object that opens and starts spewing out bullet objects, the bullet objects then have a script that deletes them when they hit another object.

The bug in question has to do with having the function known as _remove_and_delete_child()_ in multiple **if** statements. As it stands, the project will crash as soon as a bullet hits the cube, but if I changed the script to set a variable in those loops and just use remove_and_delete_child() in one place, then it will work like it should.

You will need to play the project to see it, as it would be difficult for others to confirm due to the setup needed.

This bug has been confirmed on a Win7 64 bit machine with an Ivy Bridge i7 CPU, an ATI 9xxx GPU, and 16 gigs of RAM. This using the new Godot 1.1 beta version.

title: The accelerometer does not adapt for default orientations across different android devices.
body: The x and y axes are switched between some android devices, depending on the default orientation. E.g. on device A the x axis is up and down whereas on device B the x axis is left and right, while both devices are in the same orientation. In Java, you can test for the default orientation and correct your program to match it. You can see this in the following link: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/5877780/orientation-from-android-accelerometer

title: IMPORT:: Collada importer cannot merge in newly added objects to existing scenes
body:
So essentially, assume that you're working on a scene in Blender and you export it to Collada, you import it into Godot, it loads in fine, and you set up the scene tree by assigning objects as static bodies, good right?

Now say you want to add more objects into the mix, you re-export the scene, you select the _Keep existing; Merge new_ option, but...

Godot will successfully import the changes done to the existing objects, but the new objects will not exist, Godot apparently does not know they are now in the scene file, the only way to import them is to overwrite everything and redo the scene tree setup.

So, I'm wondering if this is something that can be fixed and/or added to Godot's importing capabilities, as it would make working with large pieces of 3D scene geometry a lot easier. It would also need to recognize if an object was deleted from the file and remove it from the scene (which is also doesn't do as of now).

If this can be done for version 1.1, that would be great

thanks.

title: windows' fix for issues #1357 and #1636 : delayed MouseWheel button release events
body:
This makes BUTTON_WHEEL_UP/DOWN readable like any other mouse button
using `Input.is_mouse_button_pressed()` or `Input.is_action_pressed()`.

It simulates a delay between the "mousewheel press" event and the fake
"mousewheel release" event.

**I describe the intended behavior here, so it could be easily
reimplemented for other platforms :**

The fake release event is scheduled to occurs 100ms after the press
event, which makes it catchable into any gdscript process function (as
long as the delta is smaller than 100ms indeed).

WheelUp and WheelDown cancel each others by immediately triggering an
early release event if one was scheduled. Overlapping WheelUp and
WheelDown is thus impossible.

If several "WheelUp press" (or several "WheelDown press") events occurs
in less than 100ms, the matching release event is simply postponed to
occur 100ms after the last "wheel press" event.

The states of the BUTTON_WHEEL_UP/DOWN are also accessible through
Input.get_mouse_button_mask() respectively as bits 4 and 5.

**What behavior does it change into the Editor ?**

The only change I have noticed is that when you mouse-wheel over the 2D
or 3D viewports, it zooms in and out into two half steps instead of just
one. But this behavior was already happening before this patch. It's
just that it was not noticeable because there was no delay between the
press event and the fake release event.

**TODO (by someone else) :**
- reimplement it on Linux and MacOS
- then, add `BUTTON_MASK_WHEEL_UP = 4` and `BUTTON_MASK_WHEEL_DOWN = 5`
  into `input_event.h` and bind them into `globals_constants.cpp`.
- replace the FAKE_MOUSEWHEEL_RELEASE_DELAY_IN_TICKS constant by a
  project setting to allow to choose the fake release delay

it fixes #1357 and #1636 for windows platform only.

title: can't push_back on concatenated sub-array

Hi,

Win32 current vanilla compiled version using MSVC2010.

The func below should print : "123, 456, 789, END, 456", but instead it prints "123, 456, 456". 

This is because the two last `push_back()` have no effect on the sub-array that was used as destination for the concatenation :

```
func minimalized_failing_code(): #{

    var A = [ [123] , [456] ]

    A[ 0 ] += A[ 1 ]  # <== faulty buggy concatenation

    A[ 0 ].push_back(789)
    A[ 0 ].push_back("END")

    print( A ) # <== should print "123,456,789,END,456", but prints "123,456,456"
#}
```

If concatenate  A[0] and A[1] using a loop, it works like expected :

```
func minimalized_reference_code(): #{

    var A = [[123],[456]]

    for x in A[ 1 ]:
        A[ 0 ].push_back(x)

    A[ 0 ].push_back(789)
    A[ 0 ].push_back("END")

    print(A) # <== prints "123,456,789,END,456" like expected
#}
```

title: A large enough scene size seems to break PSSM shadows.
body:
In my game, I enlarged the total size of the scene (in terms of the max and min coordinates of the furthest vertices), and I noticed that the shadows no longer work despite the same settings working fine in levels with smaller dimensions.

I can get them to come back on by switching to the 'perspective' option, but that method doesn't work very well for many cases. I do wonder if this could be fixable by letting the position of the directional light be the center of a region where the PSSM shadow-maps are calculated (and as such shadowing will not exist beyond it). That way I can use a parenting setup to move the directional light, and as such the shadow field with the player and eliminate the distance limit (and perhaps reduce the resolution needed for decent shadows as well).

Thoughts, I think my suggestion may be possible to do with the current OpenGL-ES2 graphics.

title: Sprite.set_flip_h() now requires bool?
body:
I'm not sure when this changed, but 0 and 1 used to be automatically interpreted as boolean values by the set_flip_h function. For example, this line of code was working in older versions of Godot:

obj.set_flip_h( randi() % 2 )

But now, it must be cast to bool or the game dies when that line is hit, like so:

obj.set_flip_h( bool(randi() % 2) )

It's obviously an easy fix, but seems unnecessary since it was previously working and makes sense that it was working with 0/1 integers. I'm going to assume this applies to other functions with bool arguments, though I did not test more yet.

Was this change intentional? If it was, what was the reasoning behind it? And maybe - for cleaner code's sake - we could add a randb() which returns a random bool?

obj.set_flip_h( randb() )

title: Support for fixed process on timer (Idle/Fixed mode) and a small change for more uniform ticks
body:
- **Implemented support for fixed process on timer** 
  This is useful for cooldowns without the influence from framerate.
  The implementation is similar to animation player (idle/fixed mode), where idle mode = old timer, fixed mode = fixed process implementation:
  Example of the new behaviour with a stream of bullets with timers for each shoot on different frame rates:
  https://gfycat.com/HeartyImpressiveIndiancow
- **A change for more uniform ticks on fixed/idle**
  without this fix:
  ![0tmq6cg 1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/12376042/7554392/415ed4b8-f6f5-11e4-8acd-3af7582cc381.png)
  with this fix:
  ![3zyx16c 1](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/12376042/7554393/4ac3f7cc-f6f5-11e4-902d-6625b34e9355.png)

The change is:

> ```
>       time_left -= get_process_delta_time();
>         if (time_left<0) {
>             if (!one_shot)
>                 time_left=wait_time+time_left; //this line changed for: time_left = wait_time;
>             else
>                 stop();
>             emit_signal("timeout");
>         }
> ```

The reason for the change is:
With _time_left=wait_time+time_left;_ method: the algorithm takes on account the remaining ms from last tick for the next one, so not all ticks are the same
With _time_left = wait_time;_ method: the algorithm discards the remaining ms, so all the ticks are the same

Example of the old behaviour with a timer of 0.04 ms on a fixed framerate of 60 (~0,016 ms):

> 0,0
> 0,016
> 0,032
> 0,048
> ----- TICK on 4 frames
> 0,008
> 0,024
> 0,040
> ----- TICK on 3 frames
> 0,0
> 0,016
> 0,032
> 0,048
> ----- TICK on 4 frames

So every second tick is more fastest, resulting on non uniform behaviour between all ticks, On the fix, all the ticks start with the same value, so is always the same result (4 frames)

title: label wraps punctuation symbols individually

Curse your sudden but inevitable

title: The ability to move nodes around in the list for Organization and the ability to move nodes to different parents and shift select.
body:
I don't know about you but I like some organization in the list of my nodes. Currently, the only way to do this is to get it right the first time, which is nearly impossible with the changes that occur in a game's development. I would like the ability to grab and drop a node to a different place on the list.

Also, there isn't a way yet to move nodes to different parents. It's annoying to do a lot of work on a particular node only to realize that it would be better moved somewhere else. Now, you could copy the script over, but there's also the case of non-script based work that's don't to nodes. This isn't easily ported over. There's also the issue of dependencies, but that can be worked out. It would be great to just grab and drop nodes into different parents.

Another bit for the list UI, you can control + click to select multiple nodes, but not shift + click, which can be especially useful in larger projects.

title: Crash when powering an external sound card
body:
Hi guys
I'm not sure if the problem is caused by Godot or something else on my system, to be faire. But i'll paste the crashlog here, someone more knowledgeable might give advice.
The external soundcard is Motu UltraLite MK3 Hybrid. It is connected wiht Firewire 400 to my computer (in a FW 800 port, there is an HDD chained - the HDD doesn't seem to be any problem). 
If the soundcard is on ; then Godot crashes on launch. If i turn it on while Godot is running, Godot will crash.
For some time i have been using this soundcard with Godot without problem. One day it began crashing. Other potential culprits : Jack Audio connection kit, a Oxygen 61 MIDI keyboard, LinuxSampler, Apple XCode or commandline tools update. I installed several things at some point, and after that Godot began crashing as described.

title: Stereoscopic rendering
body:
Since Google Cardbord has appeared, more and more companies produce alike devices to make cheap VR-like experience availabile.

I wonder if it'd be possible for Godot to render stereoscopic images?

Several technologies are availabile:

Side-by-side straigth (for Google Cartboard like mounts) - left eye is left part of the screen, and vice versa.

Side-by-side inverted (for crossed-eye watching) - left eye is right part of the screen and vice versa.

Anaglyph (for oldschool 3D-glasses) - two images with altered colours are blended and displayed on top of each other, tinted glasses filter inmages for left and right eye.

Frame-interlace (for IMAX-like 3D glasses) - the images fro left and right eyes are interleaved in time, and the glasses on user's head dim the eyes to make the images go for left and right eye one at a time.

I can imagine this work for 3D games... and 2D games as well with parrarel backgrounds and overlay layers "popping out".

---

I see playing a game without having a touch interface availabile might be hard, but I've got one idea:

Using the phone with Google Cartboard for VR-like 3D display.
Using laptop/desktop PC as an input device (keyboard/mouse) transmitted via WiFi or Bluetooth to the smartphone.

title: Missing and incomplete documentation
body:
Godot's documentation is very spotty and makes learning the engine a very slow, sometimes borderline impossible process.
- The most obvious part is the fact that some features (Light Baking, Editor Plug-Ins) have remained undocumented for **more than a year**. This issue was raised in https://github.com/okamstudio/godot/issues/72, but after promises were made, nothing has changed.
- Another issue is the low quality of existing pieces of documentation. For example, the Physics and Collision (2D) tutorial doesn't explain how to use the collision triggers _at all_, it just mentions their existence and the developer is left to reverse engineer the rest with the use of example projects and forum posts.
- Some code is completely undocumented. An example would be the Path2D and PathFollow2D classes. What exactly are they meant to do? How does the developer use them?

The documentation has to be complete and up to date if the engine is meant to be usable.

title: setter sets the variable before calling the setter
body:
```
var variable= 0 setget _variable_set
func _variable_set()
    print(variable)
```

```
func _dir_set(value):
    if dir != value:

        emit_signal(SIGNAL_ANIMATE) # animator is only updated when direction is changed
```

The above code never emits because dir will always equal value.

title: AnimationTreePlayer doesn't reset non-looping animations, so they are not displayed correctly
body:
oneshot node in AnimationTrePlayer is provided to be able to add single animation,
which played once on demand blending from existing animation to that, playing it, then blending back
to previous animation. It is intended to be started as many times as necessary to replay animation.
This can be used, for example, as weapon swing animation during looped idle or walk animation - 
it swings, then gets back to original.
However now it only plays animation properly once. I'm not sure since which time, but when I am played last with AnimationTreePlayer it was working normally.

This demo application demonstractes the problem : http://ossfans.org/simple.tgz
You can open roomctl.scn and run it (no main scene setting there).
You can walk by cursor keys, jump pressing space and pressing Ctrl (left?) for 'punch' action.
The punch action plays 'punch' animation, but fails to repeat again (it looks ok only once).
If played by normal animation player, animation works fine.
You can check animations openning player.scn, selecting 'anim' node.
Script running animation is character.gd. But it all can be tested openning player.scn and pressing Start button on oneshot node named "punch".

The problem is not only with oneshot node, but with any non-looping animation.
This is broken somewhere after 1.1 if I'm not wrong.

title: accumulate mouse movement events
body: Many small mouse movement events from the window manager being processed by many Controls can slow down performance to seconds per frame territory.  These events need to be accumulated by the engine each frame, and the cumulative mouse movement sent to the Controls to process.  This could be made optional, as it might be desirable to know the _exact_ path the mouse took through each substep during the frame.

title: slow processing of input events
body:
I'm currently working on improving joystick handling, and noticed that going wild on the analog sticks dramatically reduces performance due to parsing a large number of input events.
On low end devices (2006 laptop and xperia z2) this can drop fps down to zero with even just a single gamepad.
In my code, I'm filtering out events below a user set threshold from the hardware stream. But still, having multiple devices sending out axis events can impact performance quite a bit.

According to callgrind most of the work comes from `call_group()` in `SceneTree::input_event()`

title: Area2D Reports Incorrect Collision Information Immediate After Calling set_pos()
body:
In a function if you move an Area2D via set_pos() then call get_overlapping_areas(), Godot will report the collision iteration from the previous iteration, not the current information.

I've created an example that demonstrates this behavior at http://home.comcast.net/~hammerbro/CollisionExample.zip

If you press Left, the two Area2Ds will move to the opposite ends of the screen. If you press Right, they will move to an overlapping position in the center. If you press Space Bar, the current collision information will be printed.

When you first press Right, the Area2Ds will overlap, but within that same function call they will report that they are not overlapping. If you press Space after that they will then report that they do overlap, even though they haven't moved. When you next press Left, they will report that they do overlap, even though they're no longer close to each other. Again, Space will report accurate information, but only because some number of game loops have passed since they were moved.

title: Enable jarsigner from openjdk 1.7 support
body:
I use the following script to use jarsigner from openjdk 1.7

``` shell
rm -f simple-rpg.apk simple-rpg-unaligned.apk simple-rpg-unsigned2.zip simple-rpg-unsigned2.apk
rm -Rf simple-rpg-unsigned
unzip -d simple-rpg-unsigned simple-rpg-unsigned.apk
cd simple-rpg-unsigned
rm -Rf META-INF
zip -r ../simple-rpg-unsigned2.zip *
cd ..
mv simple-rpg-unsigned2.zip simple-rpg-unsigned2.apk

jarsigner -verbose -digestalg SHA1 -sigalg MD5withRSA -keystore ~/android/release.keystore -signedjar simple-rpg-unaligned.apk simple-rpg-unsigned2.apk slapin
/home/slapin/android-sdk-linux/tools/zipalign -v 4 simple-rpg-unaligned.apk simple-rpg.apk
```

Most problems are because Godot doesn't remove signing files in templates
if these are there. You can just drop whole META-INF. Also it is easy to find on the Internet,
that jarsigner from jdk 1.7 requires the following options to work with android:
-digestalg SHA1 -sigalg MD5withRSA
digestalg also might be set to MD5.

title: Support parenting setups in Collada I/O
body:
## Currently

Godot will import the parent object, but discard the child object. This might be due to a lack of support of the import of object parenting setups in both the _better collada exporter_ and Godot's importer.
## Proposal

Support all forms of parent/child relationships in both the exporter and the importer (and have the generated nodes resemble that setup as seen in the 3D application)
## Benefits

It will make it a lot easier to create things like unique moving platforms (made just for a certain level), make it easier to create level-specific objects and allow one to increase the amount of level building work in the 3D application

I hope adding this will be seen as useful

Thanks.

title: Keep object child transform information intact when re-parenting
body:
## Currently

Re-parenting an object in the node tree will often send the newly minted child somewhere else in the level, requiring the user to find it and move it back to where it is needed.
## Proposal

Change the operation so it doesn't change the transform values of the new child object at all (the object stays exactly where it was placed).
## Benefits

It will make it much easier to reorganize parent/child hierarchies as the desired setup remains intact as nodes are moved around. Saving time and reducing frustration.

I hope this is seen as a good suggestion for the 1.2 usability release.

Thanks.

title: SIMD optimization for AABB::intersects_segment
body:
"AABB::intersects_segment" is optimized with Intel SSE instructions and runs ~2X as fast as the original.

Running:
valgrind --tool=callgrind --toggle-collect=TestAABB::test_aabb\* --cache-sim=yes --branch-sim=yes ./bin/godot.x11.64 -test aabb

then:
kcachegrind callgrind.out.*

Normal binary output shows a cycle estimation of 971474:

![KCachegrind AABB SIMD](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/12058304/9157365/b08a69fe-3eaf-11e5-913a-e0c420ead69d.png)

NOTE: Only optimized for GCC, Intel SSE, and single precision floating point!  It will compile on other platforms but won't be optimized.

title: [Discussion] Tabs and Scene tabs
body:
The purpose of this thread is to discuss the ideas and wishes around the Scene tabs of Godot editor. Multiple subjects have to be considered here and I ask every participant to quote precisely which one they relate (eg. S1 or G2).

Feel free to propose new entries for the following lists.

Considering tabs (in General) : 
- G1/ Close button : already PR-ed ( #2380 )
- G2/ Find a way to scroll horizontally over a big number of tabs
- G3/ Close tab with middle click : already PR-ed ( #2371 )

Considering scene tabs in the editor : 
- S1/ Left align the scene tabs instead of centering them.

title: Fixed multiline comments
body: Fixes multi line comments, seen in issues [#929](https://github.com/okamstudio/godot/issues/929) and [#1320](https://github.com/okamstudio/godot/issues/1320).

title: Shift + Meta + Q is a System Shortcut and Triggers Log Out on Mac OS
body: Shift + Alt + Q would be better.

title: Fix enemy.gd to actually remove dead enemies.
body: Previously, enemies sat around as invisible physics objects.  You could sometimes trip over it if it was in your way, or you could use it as a stepping stone.  I won't say the stepping stone part couldn't be interesting, but I'm fairly certain it was unintended.

title: In 3d platformer demo, remove enemies when they die.
body: Current version of platformer actually leaves dead enemies as invisible physics objects for you to trip over or use as stepping stones.  This is probably not intentional, so I wrote a simple patch that fixes it by waiting until the animation player reports being finished, then deleting the enemy.

title: File overwriting
body:
File system : 

**A.gd**:

``` GDScript
# A.gd
func _init():
    pass
```

**B.gd**:

``` GDScript
# B.gd
func _init():
    pass
```
- Open A.gd and B.gd in Godot and close them
- Rename B.gd with C.gd and A.gd with B.gd in the file system
- Reopen the files in Godot
- Here C and B have the same content, A is only available with the file system
- Close Godot, the scripts are saved and A is lost

An additional reason for don't save the unmodified scripts.

title: Set particles in state based on time
body: Right now you can set the lifetime of a Particles2D object and it will run for that amount of seconds.  However, in GDScript, there is no way to reset that timer back to the beginning or to an arbitrary time in the animation phase.  You have to wait for it to reach the lifetime and finish the animation.  This means if you want to change the parameters and options of an existing Particles2D object, you will get inconsistent results based on where it was in the previous state of animation.  Being able to set the time (or at least restart it) would be helpful.

title: Problem with Particles2D Starting On By Default?
body:
![output](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/531175/9871615/69750caa-5b5a-11e5-8d5f-835f07b3fe14.gif)

I think there's some sort of problem with Particles2D starting ON by default.  Consider the following minimal test case:

```
extends Node2D

func _ready():
    var newParticle = Particles2D.new()
    newParticle.set_pos(Vector2(200, 200))
    newParticle.set_scale(Vector2(5, 5)) #make it easier to see

    newParticle.set_explosiveness(0)
    #newParticle.set_emit_timeout(2) #this is also the default lifetime

    add_child(newParticle)
```

Here are the three conditions:

1) Initial code, particles appear

title: dict2inst return an empty instance
body:
Say you create a dictionary from an instance using `inst2dict`. Then you want to recover the instance with the values inside already defined with `dict2inst`. You're happy it worked until you find out the recovered instance has **default** values and not the ones you defined earlier.

Here's a sample:

**object.gd:**

``` GDScript
var a = 0 setget set_a,get_a
var b = 2 setget set_b,get_b

func get_a():
    return a
func set_a(v):
    a = v
func get_b():
    return b
func set_b(v):
    b = v
```

**main.gd:**

``` GDScript
var objclass = preload("res://object.gd")

func _ready():
    var obj = objclass.new()
    obj.a = 5
    obj.b = 7

    print("orig a ", obj.a) # prints 5
    print("orig b ", obj.b) # prints 7

    var dictVal = inst2dict(obj)

    print("dict a ", dictVal.a) # prints 5
    print("dict b ", dictVal.b) # prints 7

    var instVal = dict2inst(dictVal)

    print("inst a ", instVal.a) # prints 0
    print("inst b ", instVal.b) # prints 2
```

title: [Feature Request] Possibility to create scenes with root node from external file
body:
It's impossible to have node from external file as a root node. In our game we use couple of hacks to bypass that limitation but they create another problems and are generally troublesome. 
Why I think there should be this possibility? Because it's easier to do hierarchical objects structure thanks to this, (just like in object oriented programming, but with scenes). **Maybe I will give real life example here.**

Let's say we will have enemies in our game, quite a lot of them most of them very similar to each other. We could create one scene "BaseEnemy" write a script there, add a lot of inner nodes that are needed for this code to work and setup nice amount of export variables (thanks to them we will be able to modify individual enemies behaviour):
![baseenemy](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/6129594/9976058/4cb2e910-5ed5-11e5-9918-d482628fa555.png)
_A base enemy scene_

Then for each concrete enemy we cloud just simply load BaseEnemy as root node, setup exported values of Enemy and decorate it with additional specific nodes that are needed like model asset, or additional weapon. 
![concreteenemy](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/6129594/9976059/516670c6-5ed5-11e5-9250-903b202b4499.png)
_A concrete enemy scene_

Now when we need to change some shared node/logic of our enemy in some way, we don't need to update 10 files separately, we only need to update that single "BaseEnemy.xscn" one :) 

I think that this simple feature would make life of at least some of us a lot easier :) What do you think? 
(Off course I mean "simple" from user side, not sure if this feature would not force another scene format change, but hey! They have changed already between current and 1.1 so it could be good time for this :)

title: Can't Press TextureButtons with Negative Scale
body:
If you have a TextureButton with a scale whose x or y contains a negative value, you can't click on it.

To demonstrate this, take an empty project, create two TextureButtons, one named "Normal" and the other named "Flipped". Set their Normal texture to whatever you'd like (I used the default icon.png for both), then add the following code to the scene:

```
func _ready():
    get_node("Normal").connect("pressed", self, "button_pressed")
    get_node("Flipped").set_scale(Vector2(1, -1))
    get_node("Flipped").connect("pressed", self, "button_pressed")

func button_pressed():
    print("A button was pressed.")
```

The print statement will happen for the Normal button but not for the Flipped button. This seems to happen regardless of whether the scale was set in the editor or via code, as long as at least one of the values is negative. Things work fine with arbitrary positive values.

When the tree structure is like (assume all nodes are `Node2D`s):

```
common_root
  some_parent_A
    node_A
  some_parent_B
    node_B
```

`node_A.get_relative_transform(node_B)` will error at [node2d.cpp:342](https://github.com/okamstudio/godot/blob/d3eb9e8c54d4a93b2bed90a5988f9814377d409f/scene/2d/node_2d.cpp#L342), and return `node_A`'s global transform instead.

Note: This can't be reproduced like:

```
common_root
  node_A
  node_B
```

, because then the `if` at line 343 would work properly.

title: Add all collision shapes to a tile when converting scenes to TileSets
body:
Currently when converting a scene to a `TileSet`, only the first shape of each `StaticBody2D` is added to the tile.
For multiple shapes, one has to add multiple `StaticBody2D` nodes and give one shape to each.
For concave `CollisionPolygon2D` nodes in `BUILD_SOLIDS` mode, which split the concave polygon shape into multiple convex polygon shapes, only the first shape is added to the tile, making it impossible to use `CollisionPolygon2D` for concave polygons.

This change has all shapes added to the tile when converting.

Fixes #2331

title: Fix default StyleBoxes of MenuButton
body:
The focus mode of MenuButton nodes is by default set to `FOCUS_NONE`. However, when the focus mode is changed, MenuButton falls back to the ERROR texture, since the `focus` StyleBox is not set in the default theme.
This happens in some MenuButton instances in the editor, such as the animation player "Tracks" button (see #729).

This change adds the `sb_button_focus` StyleBox for MenuButton. I think this looks alright, but a designer (@ndee85?) might want to take a look at it. In any case, this gets rid of the ugly ERROR texture.

Fixes #729.

title: Fix arguments parsing in the main function
body:
Fixes #2611 which was a regression from 692216b86ab97db91e7ff3903ffc9ac8e37433f6.
The bogus behaviour considered that if there were more than one arguments left to parse,
they would be a pair of arguments (switch and its parameter), and thus skipped the next
argument in all cases (thus potentially skipping a "-editor", which triggered #2611).

This is fixed by checking first for arguments that don't expect a parameter, and only
afterwards for arguments that expect a parameter. And if a "pair" of arguments is not
valid, we no longer increment the counter.

title: Scrolling Control nodes don't display correctly when under a Render Target viewport
body:
I'm still using 1.1 but I tested this in a recent release of 2.0 and it was still an issue.

When using a Render Target viewport (such as when using `stretch_mode`, `viewport`) I've found that ScrollContainer nodes and RichTextLabel nodes have some offset not behaving or something. (There might be other types that have this issue, these are the ones I've found). I'll try to illustrate...

I put a few Control nodes under a Render Target viewport and few above it and this is what it SHOULD look like
![howitshouldlook](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/15483613/11039252/5302dbee-86cc-11e5-804b-e88e515e5411.png)

However this is what it does instead
![output](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/15483613/11039034/729ed33c-86cb-11e5-9d0d-427f6353399f.png)

The white/black squares are texture frames and are working correctly. The white ones are children of the Render Target viewport and the black ones are not but they just show that they line up as intended.

The red box, the green box with the gradient, and the second (not visible) RichTextLabel are all children of a Render Target viewport, the  blue box, the first box with the image of the gradient, and the first RichTextLabel are not. In fact, here's what the scene looks like...
![scene](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/15483613/11039466/6f5768fe-86cd-11e5-97a7-f00e67a43990.png)

I actually just used a big `draw_rect` to locate the wandering nodes. At first it appeared as though the nodes just weren't showing up at all.

Also worth mentioning that I forgot to show is that the boxes move when the window is resized. If the window is resized just a little they'll move down a little more. They move out of the window entirely before it's even twice as tall. And it's just like... the clipping rectangle that moves. For example, in the green box with the gradient image, the image and scroll bar will stay where they are, the visible area will just move so that it shows less and less of them.

title: draw_line() operates on global coords but accepts local coords
body:
**Preface:**  
draw_line() and draw_polygon() and draw_circle() do not provide the prettiest. outputs and can cause aliasing.  An attempt to emulate subpixel drawing failed.

**Issue:**  
draw_line() will snap to global coordinates, but accepts local coords.  This can cause some unexpected behavior as lines snap to unexpected coordinates.

**Expected behavior:**  
draw_line() should round() inputs rather than floor() or ceil() them.  Alternatively, if draw_line() is called for width 1 at x = 0.5, two lines are drawn at x=0 and x=1 with alpha of approximately 0.5 \* rgba.  (I personally found alpha of pow( 1 - (x-floor(x)), 2) and pow( 1 - (x-ceil(x)), 2) to be pleasing.)  Using alpha to provide smother draw_polygon() and draw_circle() outputs would also be desired.

**Example**:
    extends Sprite

   set_pos(Vector2(100.1,100)
    var x = 0.5
    draw_line( Vector2(floor(x), 0), Vector2(floor(x), 20) ) # line is drawn at x = 100
    draw_line( Vector2(ceil(x), 0), Vector2(ceil(x), 20) ) # line is drawn at x = 102

![](http://i.imgur.com/Fz1qM2I.png)
**Image explaination:**  
draw_line() is used twice for each 10% interval of the bar length with alpha scaled to represent how close the line is to the floor(x) or ceil(x).  The third line has a 1 pixel gap.

title: Auto bracket completion is disabled when a new script is created
body:
Auto bracket completion enables the editor to add a right bracket automatically after a left bracket was typed. 

How to reproduce:
- Enable auto bracket completion in Settings/Editor Settings/TextEditor/Auto Brace Complete.
- Create a scene, add a root node (whatever you want)
- Create a new script on this node. Built-in or not built-in has no impact.
- Try to type a left bracket

Expected:
- A right bracket should appear next to the left bracket.

Workaround:
- In Settings/Editor Settings, disable TextEditor/Auto Brace Complete, then re-enable it immediately.
- Auto bracket completion now works.
- Every time a new script is created, this behaviour happens.

BY THE WAY, this functionality should be enabled by default. It is currently disabled by default.

title: Send a text without godot serialization.
body:
#2863

Test file .gd

```

extends Node

var server

func _ready():
    set_process(true)
    var port = 5555
    server = TCP_Server.new()

    if server.listen( port ) == 0:
        print("Server started on port " + str(port) )
        set_process( true )
    else:
        print( "Failed to start server on port " + str(port) )

func _process( delta ):
    if server.is_connection_available(): # check if someone's trying to connect
        var client = server.take_connection() # accept connection
        var rs = ""
        var cache = ""
        var end = false
        while(!end):
            cache += client.get_data(1)[1].get_string_from_utf8()
            #check end of line
            if(cache.substr(cache.length()-2,cache.length()) == "\r\n"):
                #check begin with \r\n -> end of stream
                if(cache.length()==2):
                    end = true
                else:#next line
                    rs += cache
                    cache = ""
        print(rs)
        print( "Client has connected!" )
        client.put_text( "HTTP/1.1 200 Ok\n" + "Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8\n" + "Content-Length: 0\n" + "Connection: close\n" + "\r\n" )
        client.disconnect()
```

title: Export named flags property with GDScript
body:
The Texture resource has a "Flags" property in which you can select multiple elements in a list. There's no current way to export such a property via GDScript.

![godot-named-flags](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/5599796/11593971/7caad412-9a8e-11e5-895c-2b0a5f52f92a.png)

I suggest to expand in the current flags property format:

``` GDScript
# This is the current format for flags, like the CanvasItem's Light Mask property:
export(int, FLAGS) var current_flags

# Suggested format for named flags:
export(int, FLAGS, "Name 1", "Name 2", "And so on") var named_flags
```

It should be relatively easy to add this, just a careful change in the GDScript parser to accept `PROPERTY_HINT_FLAGS` near the [place where it parses the `PROPERTY_HINT_ALL_FLAGS`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/064fd762fae75371658e773a3acf39616e813b08/modules/gdscript/gd_parser.cpp#L2380-L2389).

title: define BACK_TO_TABLES in aes256.cpp?
body:
Is there a reason the line
# define BACK_TO_TABLES

is commented out at the top of core/io/aes256.cpp?  From what I can gather, the current code skips the use of lookup tables, and instead calculates the needed data on the fly.  In my roughly measured experiments where I enabled encryption of my scripts, this gives me load times 3-4 times longer than the unencrypted scripts.  If I uncomment this line, so that it uses the lookup tables, I can no longer distinguish between the encrypted and unencrypted load times, which is great.  But I wonder if this is too good to be true, and using the lookup tables is a bad choice for some reason.  I was able to export my scripts encrypted using a slow, non-lookup table built binary, then load that data using the fast lookup table version, so it seems they both work correctly.

Shall I make a PR for this, enabling the lookup tables?  Does anyone know enough about this to comment on whether this is a good idea?  I should be able to do this through scons build scripts myself, but if this is an acceptable change, I see no reason to keep doing it the slow way by default.

title: Instant segfault when parsing subclass
body:
As of commit 4028dfa, a subclass present in a singleton causes an instant, non-informative segmentation fault running a project or opening the editor.
Running gdb only returns 

```
Program received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
0x000000000049620c in GDCompiler::_parse_class(GDScript*, GDScript*, GDParser::ClassNode const*) ()
```

on an Ubuntu 15.10 64b system. gcc (Ubuntu 5.2.1-22ubuntu2) 5.2.1 20151010.

The class in question is merely 

```
class Char:
    var stats = {
        vital = 0,
        ep = 0,
        over = 0,
        ad = 0,
        lp = 0
    }
```

and removing/commenting it starts godot normally. (_This used to work until this commit_). 
I don't know if this is a behavior unique to singletons or a general problem in the class parser, though, I don't have any example of subclasses elsewhere.

title: Enhancing Godot Engine :)
body:
- Add a viewer to Project's root node hierarchical relationship to all referenced nodes in the project.
  When the project grows, finding the relationship between scenes becomes awkward and hard to maintain.
  By adding a Project mode, "Scene" like tab to show heirarchy of the object (a ListTree would suffice).
  It would make working with Godot more robust than ever.

In the Instancing wiki tutorial: see the following image.
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/wiki/images/shooter_instancing.png

If Godot can show this kind of relationship between scenes it would be awesome.

I am coming from Game Maker Studio Pro, and I really hate to compare it with Godot since both
are excellent, and both have different ways of doing the management. But at least Game Maker Studio
does have excellent project viewer. It even creates logical filter "Folders" for resources or Rooms (Scenes) in the Project's ListTree.

Please consider adding this feature.
- When renaming any kind of object in Godot, it should find all occurrences in scripts/editor
  and change that as well. This can be achieved by parsing script files, any matching names for the changed 
  scene/node, like "load(), preload(), set_script() get_node()..etc!) functions.
- There is an awesome library called "stb_image" https://github.com/nothings/stb
  It is a single header library, no license at all, can be used without any creditation.
  Basically they are Public Domain, it has great number of file formats.

There are other header files too in that project to open OggVorbis, TrueType fonts...etc
also public domain.
- Please consider adding more image formats, a vectorized SWF file would be awesome.
  To avoid pixelated images while zooming.
- I know I am stretching it, but it would be great if the users would be able to create a
  breakpoint by clicking  the area left to line numbers by making it a few pixels wider 
  (similar to Visual Studio), also adding a context menu to create custom breakpoint 
  that occurs when a condition is true, for example (only do a breakpoint `if x value > 30`)

Thanks for the great work on Godot, you guys are awesome.

title: Suggestion: Multiple Scripts
body:
I'm unsure if this has been discussed and dismissed, but I think this engine would benefit from allowing objects to run multiple scripts. As far as I am aware there is no feature for this but correct me if I am wrong.

I feel like this would be a very good way to separate functionality and keep devs from having to create scripts that might combine behaviour they have already written. Like for example, if you want an enemy that has the same AI as the basic enemy but needs some special functionality like enhanced AI for given scenarios, it might help to just add a smaller script containing the extended AI features rather than a longer script containing the basic AI mixed with the enhanced AI. This is not currently my issue and I do realize this problem can be solved by using Godot's current scripting solution, however I feel like this feature would help modulate scripts for better project management.

Let me know what you think,
thanks for reading.
